common_name: Veitchii Skimmia (Heavy-Berrying Female Evergreen Shade Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; site a male Skimmia such as 'Rubella' or 'Fragrans' nearby, since 'Veitchii' is a female clone and needs cross-pollination to set its heavy berry crop.

directions: Veitchii is a long-established, RHS Award of Garden Merit female Skimmia japonica selection grown for an exceptionally heavy, reliable set of glossy red berries that hang on through winter above dense, dark-green, aromatic evergreen foliage. Small clusters of star-shaped, creamy-white flowers open in mid to late spring and must be cross-pollinated by a male Skimmia growing within about fifteen feet to produce fruit. It is slower and slightly more tolerant of sun than many Skimmia cultivars, but still colors and grows best out of hot afternoon exposure, and it is notably tolerant of urban pollution and neglect once established. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist, acidic to neutral soil, mulch annually to preserve soil acidity, and prune only lightly to remove damaged wood, since flowers and berries form on the previous year's growth.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society — Skimmia japonica 'Veitchii' (AGM plant)
Hillier Manual of Trees and Shrubs

common_name: Mountain Snow Pieris (Heat-Tolerant Compact Bronze New-Growth Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to partial sun; Mountain Snow was bred for improved heat tolerance, making it a better choice than older Pieris japonica cultivars in warmer parts of its range.

directions: Mountain Snow is a compact, heat-improved Pieris japonica selection valued for pendant chains of ivory-white, urn-shaped flower buds that form in summer and persist ornamentally through winter before opening in early spring, paired with new spring growth that emerges a warm bronze-red rather than the flame-red of older cultivars. Its dense, rounded habit and improved tolerance of summer heat make it a more reliable choice than the straight species in the warmer half of its hardiness range, while still performing well in colder gardens. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5–6.5) soil in partial shade to morning sun with afternoon shade, and mulch to conserve moisture and soil acidity. Prune only lightly right after flowering if needed, since next year's buds set soon after bloom finishes.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection — Mountain Snow Pieris
North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox

common_name: Brouwer's Beauty Pieris (Cold-Hardy Japonica-Floribunda Hybrid Andromeda)
scientific_name: Pieris 'Brouwer's Beauty' (P. japonica x P. floribunda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; Brouwer's Beauty is a hybrid of native Pieris floribunda and Japanese Pieris japonica bred for superior cold hardiness and resistance to lace bugs.

directions: Brouwer's Beauty combines the greater cold-hardiness and upright, lace-bug-resistant character of native Pieris floribunda with the larger, glossier foliage of Pieris japonica, a hybrid selected at Brouwer Nursery in New Jersey that has since earned a Cary Award for outstanding performance in New England gardens. Deep purplish-red flower buds form in fall and stand out through winter before opening in early spring into upright to horizontal trusses of creamy-white, urn-shaped, lightly fragrant flowers. Its dense, slow-growing, rounded habit and tolerance of colder winters than most Pieris japonica cultivars make it a dependable choice for foundation plantings and shrub borders in regions where other Pieris struggle. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds form on the current season's growth soon after bloom.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox — Pieris 'Brouwer's Beauty'
University of New Hampshire Extension — Cary Award plants

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Leucothoe keiskei is a dwarf Japanese species distinct from the more commonly planted L. fontanesiana and L. axillaris, valued for shining red new shoots and unusually large flowers for the genus.

directions: Introduced from Japan by plant collector Ernest Wilson in 1915, Leucothoe keiskei is a dwarf, slow-spreading evergreen shrub with slender, zigzagging stems distinct in scale and character from the larger, more common drooping and coast leucothoes. New shoots emerge a shining red before maturing to glossy dark green, and the narrow, pointed leaves flush deep red again in autumn and winter, giving it multi-season color on a compact frame well suited to the front of a shaded border or a woodland rock garden. In midsummer it produces nodding, pure-white, cylindrical flowers noticeably larger than those of other cultivated leucothoes, held in short clusters near the shoot tips. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade sheltered from hot afternoon sun and drying winds, and mulch to conserve moisture; established plants need little routine care beyond removing occasional damaged stems.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)
